methods.name: Kahn’s algorithm
methods.title: Topological Sorting of Large Networks
methods.version: Publication 1962
methods.model: Static directed graph; each prerequisite must precede its dependent.
methods.output: One valid order, or cycle failure.
methods.goal: Find any valid topological order.
methods.mechanism: Select tasks with no unfinished prerequisites, then update their successors.
methods.strength: Simple dependency handling; linear traversal with adjacency lists.
methods.limitation: A valid order is not necessarily the best order for storage or runtime.
methods.change: Remove zero-indegree vertices and release their successors.
methods.relevance: Preserve eligibility and optimize only added priority bookkeeping. A faster byte-priority implementation does not improve the linear FIFO bound.
methods.guarantee: R(D) = {v not in D : every predecessor of v is in D}.
methods.guarantee_note: Only vertices in R(D) may be selected. Removing one ready vertex and decreasing its successors’ indegrees preserves that condition. If output stops before all vertices appear, the graph is cyclic.
methods.time: O(n + m) with adjacency lists and a constant-time FIFO queue.
methods.space: O(n) extra state, beyond the graph.
methods.code:
73  def fifo_kahn(successors: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
 74      """P1: source removal. Input rows must contain valid, unique endpoints."""
 75      degree = indegrees(successors)
 76      ready = deque(v for v, d in enumerate(degree) if d == 0)
 77      order: list[int] = []
 78      while ready:
 79          u = ready.popleft()                 # P1a: eligible task only
 80          order.append(u)
 81          for v in successors[u]:
 82              degree[v] -= 1                 # P1b: one removed predecessor
 83              if degree[v] == 0:
 84                  ready.append(v)
 85      if len(order) != len(successors):
 86          raise ValueError("cycle detected")
 87      return tuple(order)

questions.title: When is extra analysis worth its cost?
questions.question: Which measured workflow property separates useful preparation from overhead?
questions.evidence: Some reviewed schedulers spend substantially more time constructing a schedule; a reduction must repay its preparation cost.
questions.test: Profile two development workflows. Look for a crossover and a no-benefit case before designing a rule.
questions.boundary: An arbitrary cutoff or the word adaptive is not an original contribution.

questions.title: How much work finds a genuinely changed priority?
questions.question: How often does the scheduler inspect an entry whose priority has not changed?
questions.evidence: Tagged XLA code already refreshes priorities following a last-use transition. The affected-entry search itself is a separate cost.
questions.test: Count examined entries and actual changes in a competent implementation. Preserve its next-task decision.
questions.boundary: Updating only changed priorities is already known. A specific additional difference is required.

questions.title: Does representation cost more than the decision?
questions.question: Are lookups, copied metadata, or queue traffic responsible for the measured bottleneck?
questions.evidence: The September 2026 OpenXLA change already uses dense indices and shared ranges. Locality studies report workload-dependent effects.
questions.test: Profile memory access and setup separately from score evaluation. Compare with the indexed-state precedent.
questions.boundary: A simple array substitution or shared-range layout is not a new contribution here.

questions.title: Which Montage structure supports a narrow claim?
questions.question: Does a recurring dependency pattern explain unnecessary work, and when is the pattern absent?
questions.evidence: Montage metadata describes producers, consumers and prerequisites; cleanup pruning already exploits precedence.
questions.test: Define the pattern on development traces, then check held-out cases and a counterexample without it.
questions.boundary: Application specialization alone is not novelty. Do not remove uncertified dependencies.

questions.title: Are we comparing the same problem?
questions.question: Which assumptions must stay fixed for a runtime difference to mean an implementation improvement?
questions.evidence: Dynamic ordering, cache management and compiler scheduling have different outputs and execution models.
questions.test: Write one shared input, output, priority and timing contract. Put incompatible studies in context, not in a winner ranking.
questions.boundary: Different hardware or a different objective cannot substantiate the same-policy speed claim.

questions.title: What would make the idea fail?
questions.question: Which small legal workflow would expose a wrong decision or erase the expected saving?
questions.evidence: Greedy scheduling is not globally optimal; prior comparisons contain workload-dependent gains and regressions.
questions.test: Build one adversarial correctness case and one no-benefit case. Check both score equality and total runtime.
questions.boundary: Finite tests supplement a proof; fewer counter operations do not guarantee lower runtime.

questions.title: Does the cost matter on the actual workload?
questions.question: Which operation dominates complete order construction after all simple baseline optimizations?
questions.evidence: Horizons measures metadata construction separately; XLA already removes representation work.
questions.test: Profile the two development workflows, including setup, without selecting a method first.
questions.boundary: A lower counter count alone is not a runtime improvement; do not select only favorable cases.

questions.title: Are these methods solving the same problem?
questions.question: Does a result still apply when one output has several consumers or when the required task order is fixed?
questions.evidence: Peak-memory tractability changes with the lifetime model; recent optimizers may alter the ordering policy.
questions.test: Write the input, output and release semantics beside each proposed baseline before implementing it.
questions.boundary: Use unlike methods as context, not as a numerical ranking or a claimed missing feature.

questions.title: What finding would make us reject the idea?
questions.question: Which workload or cost measurement could show that the modification is unnecessary or too expensive?
questions.evidence: Published tracking improvements include unfavorable thresholds and workload-dependent effects.
questions.test: Predeclare a no-benefit case and include all selected inputs and timing repetitions.
questions.boundary: Unfavorable results are evidence to retain, not grounds for removing the case.

"""Timing harness for validated Workflow objects. The CLI uses SYNTHETIC data.

No speedup claim is supplied with this template. To test Montage, first map a
frozen trace into Workflow and validate the producer and consumer semantics.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import gc
import json
import platform
import random
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
from time import perf_counter_ns
from workflow_methods import (Workflow, per_file_groups, aggregate_equal,
    reduce_consumers, direct_certificates, incremental)
from run_checks import fixture


def benchmark(w: Workflow, repetitions: int = 20, budget: int = 8) -> dict:
    if repetitions < 2:
        raise ValueError("use at least two repetitions")
    w.validate()  # Common validation, not an unreported proposed-method cost.
    def execute(name: str):
        groups = per_file_groups(w)  # Method preparation starts here.
        if name == "equal_consumers":
            groups = aggregate_equal(groups)
        elif name == "direct_certificates":
            groups = direct_certificates(w, groups).groups
        elif name == "full_maximal":
            groups = reduce_consumers(w, groups, None).groups
        elif name == "bounded":
            groups = reduce_consumers(w, groups, budget).groups
        return incremental(w, groups, audit=False)
    names = ["per_file", "equal_consumers", "direct_certificates", "full_maximal", "bounded"]
    for name in names:
        execute(name)  # Identical warm-up count; do not reuse mutable state.
    times = {name:[] for name in names}
    counts = {}
    rng = random.Random(20261014)
    for _ in range(repetitions):
        order = names.copy()
        rng.shuffle(order)
        for name in order:
            gc.collect()
            enabled = gc.isenabled()
            gc.disable()
            try:
                start = perf_counter_ns()
                result = execute(name)
                elapsed = perf_counter_ns() - start
            finally:
                if enabled:
                    gc.enable()
            times[name].append(elapsed)
            counts[name] = result.counter_decrements
    return {"python":platform.python_version(), "platform":platform.platform(),
            "runs_per_method":repetitions, "budget_edge_inspections":budget,
            "raw_time_ns":times, "median_time_ns":{k:median(v) for k,v in times.items()},
            "counter_decrements":counts,
            "scope":"Includes grouping, searches, initialization, and order construction. "
                    "Excludes common input validation, parsing, and debug score histories."}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--runs",type=int,default=20)
    parser.add_argument("--out",type=Path,default=Path("synthetic_timing.json"))
    args=parser.parse_args()
    result=benchmark(fixture("ordered consumers"),args.runs)
    result["input_kind"]="synthetic demonstration, NOT Montage"
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\n")
    print(f"Wrote synthetic demonstration measurements to {args.out}")

def random_workflow(seed: int) -> Workflow:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = rng.randint(2, 18)
    labels = list(range(n))
    rng.shuffle(labels)  # IDs do not encode the topological order.
    succ = [set() for _ in range(n)]
    for i, u in enumerate(labels):
        for v in labels[i+1:]:

                succ[u].add(v)
    files: list[File] = []
    for j in range(rng.randint(n, 3*n)):

        p = labels[p_pos]

        cs = frozenset(v for v in choices if rng.random() < 0.40)
        if files and rng.random() < 0.23:

            cs = frozenset(v for v in rng.choice(files).consumers if v in choices)
        succ[p].update(cs)  # Preserve every producer-before-consumer condition.
        files.append(File(f"f{j}", p, cs, rng.choice((0,1,2,5,11,29))))
    files.append(File("external_input", None, frozenset(labels[::2]), 97))

def compare(w: Workflow) -> dict:
    w.validate()
    oracle = recompute(w)
    base = per_file_groups(w)
    plans = {
        "per_file": (base, 0),
        "equal_consumers": (aggregate_equal(base), 0),

        assert actual.ready_scores == oracle.ready_scores, (name, "different ready scores")

def exhaustive_cover_check() -> dict:
    """All 64 forward-edge DAGs on four consumers; all valid set reductions.

    For each graph, every nonempty C, every nonempty S subset C covering C by
    reachability, and every downward-closed completed set D are checked. Tests
    evaluate every ready vertex. This is finite evidence, not a universal proof.
    """
    n = 4
    universe = set(range(n))
    arcs = [(u,v) for u in range(n) for v in range(u+1,n)]
    triples = checks = reductions = 0
    for mask in range(1 << len(arcs)):
        edges = [e for j,e in enumerate(arcs) if mask & (1 << j)]
        reach = [set() for _ in range(n)]
        for u,v in edges:
            reach[u].add(v)
        for u in reversed(range(n)):
            for v in tuple(reach[u]):
                reach[u].update(reach[v])
        states = []
        for bits in range(1 << n):
            done = {v for v in range(n) if bits & (1 << v)}
            if any(v in done and u not in done for u,v in edges):
                continue
            ready = {v for v in universe-done
                     if all(u in done for u,x in edges if x == v)}
            states.append((done,ready))
        for c_bits in range(1, 1 << n):
            cs = {v for v in universe if c_bits & (1 << v)}
            for s_bits in range(1, 1 << n):
                kept = {v for v in universe if s_bits & (1 << v)}
                if not kept <= cs:
                    continue
                if any(not (reach[c] & kept) for c in cs-kept):
                    continue
                reductions += 1
                for done,ready in states:
                    triples += 1
                    for v in ready:
                        original = v in cs and cs-done == {v}
                        reduced = v in kept and kept-done == {v}
                        assert original == reduced
                        checks += 1
    return {"forward_edge_graphs":64, "consumer_set_reductions":reductions,
            "completed_set_configurations":triples,
            "ready_credit_equalities_checked":checks, "passed":True}

        File("final_A",0,frozenset(),1),
        File("temporary_B",1,frozenset((2,)),2),
        File("final_C",2,frozenset(),1)))
    w.validate()
    greedy = recompute(w).order
    candidates = [(peak_retained_bytes(w,tuple(p)),tuple(p))
                  for p in itertools.permutations(range(w.n))
                  if valid_order(w,tuple(p))]
    optimum = min(candidates)
    peak = peak_retained_bytes(w,greedy)
    assert greedy == (0,1,2) and peak == 4 and optimum[0] == 3
    return {"greedy_order":greedy, "greedy_peak":peak,
            "best_order":optimum[1], "optimal_peak":optimum[0],
            "valid_orders_enumerated":len(candidates),
            "all_order_peaks":candidates,
            "model":"synthetic retained bytes; allocate outputs before input release"}

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)

    exhaustive = exhaustive_cover_check()
    negative = negative_controls()
    counterexample = greedy_counterexample()
    for seed in range(args.cases):

    result = {"run_date":"2026-10-14", "python":platform.python_version(),
              "random_workflows":args.cases, "seeds":[0,args.cases-1],

nodes.relationship: Kahn cites Lasser as earlier work

nodes.limitation: A valid order alone does not optimize retained storage or task execution time.

nodes.year: Standard form; no origin date assigned

nodes.title: DFS reverse postorder
nodes.relationship: Sibling static algorithm, not a Kahn extension

nodes.relationship: Explicit modification of the AHRSZ approach
